references.text: The prophecy that God's people will flee from foreign shepherds and not know their voice is a direct fulfillment of Ezekiel's warning against the bad shepherds who lead the people astray.
Ezekiel predicts that the Lord himself will raise up a shepherd (David) whom the people will follow, in contrast to the foreigners they flee from in John 10.
Isaiah describes the bad shepherds as those who do not understand and who lead the people away, a direct parallel to the foreigners whom the people flee because they do not know their voice.
